submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE (0.00106%) came from index 26, the Sb-richest composition (Sb 0.757). There, an Sb-rich phase such as MgSb4O10 (MEGNet HSE gap 1.2 eV) can absorb the 2.7 eV light, and XRD shows a secondary phase. EQE rose with Sb content: index 13 gave about 0, index 23 gave 0.00043%, index 26 gave 0.00106%.

rejected.reason: MgSb2O6 stoichiometry, predicted gap 2.82 eV; measured EQE 0.00043%, lower than index 26
Mid-range composition; measured EQE is essentially zero (-0.00006%). Likely Mg4Sb2O9 (4.2 eV gap) plus MgO, which barely absorbs
Mg3SbO4 is 0.50 eV/atom above hull; the phases that do form there (MgO, Mg4Sb2O9) have gaps well above 2.7 eV

consultations.verdict: Support: MgSb2O6 (mp-3653) HSE gap 2.82 eV, nearest to 2.7 eV photon; MgSb2O4 3.34 and Mg4Sb2O9 4.23 eV too wide. Sb-rich end most promising; index 23 is at MgSb2O6 stoichiometry.

Support: Sb-rich MgSb4O10 (mp-2232528) HSE gap 1.21 eV absorbs 2.7 eV light; Mg3SbO4 3.07 eV would not. Index 26 (Sb 0.757) is closest to the Sb-rich phase and XRD shows extra peaks (secondary phase). Index 23 EQE was negligible, so move to Sb-rich end.

Mostly against the Mg-rich side: Mg3SbO4 is 0.50 eV/atom above hull (it won't form), so Mg-rich films are likely Mg4Sb2O9 (4.2 eV gap) + MgO, which won't absorb well. Index 26 is already the Sb-rich edge, and measuring 24/25 would add little. So I'm using the last measurement as an exploratory hedge on the unmeasured middle of the line (index 13, Sb 0.38), where the GP is most uncertain.
